about: Two comparisons and no search. `b`'s demand sits under `a`'s, and
`a`'s limit under `b`'s — the direction reverses between the two
marks, and an implementation that compares both the same way passes
the reflexive cases and fails the rest.
The product order: a non-maximal cross does not explode. Only the
strongest cross (top floor, bottom ceiling) still entails every

coverage.criterion: reflexive, strictly narrower each way, incomparable, and an unsatisfiable statement on both sides
coverage.why: one scale for the named cases; over every pair of the chain's twenty-five statements entails is checked against the product order, and a conjunction against each of its parts

cases.name: wider ceiling does not entail narrower
lower floor does not entail higher
a cross below the strongest does not entail another: crosses are ordered, not one bottom

orders.name: M2 — a non-canonical cross, the case the chain never asked

cases.name: the strongest cross still entails an inhabited pair
non-canonical cross does not entail an inhabited incomparable pair
an inhabited one does not entail a non-canonical cross
two non-canonical crosses do not entail each other

product: entails is the product order: over the chain's twenty-five pairs of a floor and a ceiling, a entails b exactly when b's floor sits under a's and a's ceiling under b's
composition: a conjunction entails each of its parts, over every pair of inhabited statements on the chain
